subject: MAP: Decision rubric, acceptance tests & sprint timeline
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Steele <naomi.steele@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: Decision rubric, acceptance tests & sprint timeline

Hi Naomi —

Following our call last week, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that organizes the evaluation into a compact 2-week sprint with clear exit gates and pass/fail acceptance tests. High-level summary below; full workbook attached (redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx) and acceptance rules are in acceptance_tests.yml.

Key success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: P95 generation latency <= 350ms for clinical summarization flows (3k context)
- Quality: Automated ROUGE-L / BLEU benchmarks + 20 curated prompts: >= 90% parity vs baseline (human-reviewed)
- Cost: Per-session token cost < $0.06 (hosted profile with caching enabled)
- Reliability: 99.5% successful completions under target throughput (10 rps)

Exit gates and acceptance tests (high level):
1) Sandbox validation (3 days) — model runs, KV cache verification, tokens sanity checks
2) Integration smoke (2 days) — sample patient data run, no PII leakage, KMS logging validated
3) QA pass (4 days) — 20 prompt set, human spot-check; <= 2 critical regressions
4) Production readiness signoff (1 day) — contract SOW & SLA agreed

Proposed timeline (two-week sprint):
- Week 1: Sandbox validation + Integration smoke
- Week 2: QA pass + Final metrics review and signoff

Asks from StellarHealth: please confirm the following by EOD Friday (Nov 13):
- Which internal QA lead will own human spot-checks (name + email)
- Any additional compliance tests (e.g., HIPA A/B) to include in acceptance_tests.yml
- Whether we should run on Dedicated capacity or Hosted evaluation profile (we recommend Hosted for speed)

Attachments: redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook), acceptance_tests.yml (detailed pass/fail rules)

Thanks — happy to tighten thresholds based on your QA cadence.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP: Decision rubric, acceptance tests & sprint timeline

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the MAP — this is exactly the structure we were hoping for. A few clarifying items from our side before we lock thresholds: 

- Human QA: I'll own human spot-checks and will loop in Sandra Lopez (sandra.lopez@stellarhealth.com) — she runs our clinical review bench.
- Compliance: We need an explicit PII scrub verification step and a logging check against our KMS stamps; can you add an automated proof-of-redaction job (sample size ~200 docs) to acceptance_tests.yml?
- Capacity: For the evaluation sprint we prefer Hosted evaluation profile first; if latency looks good we'll switch to a Dedicated probe.

One change request on thresholds: P95 <= 350ms is aggressive for our 3k prompts — would you accept P95 <= 450ms as a candidate gate, with an improvement plan to 350ms within 30 days post-procurement?

Can we aim to kick off the sandbox validation week of Nov 22? We need internal calendar time to provision test accounts.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Steele
Director, Clinical Integrations
StellarHealth

Subject: Finalized MAP & acceptance rubric — signoff requested by Nov 18

Hi Naomi —

Appreciate the quick review and the confirmation on timelines. Per our internal alignment (Markus/Aditya), I updated the MAP and acceptance rules with the following final items: 

Final acceptance gates (condensed):
- Sandbox (Days 1–3): basic model runs, KV cache, token sanity checks, PII scrub job (sample 200) — must pass
- Integration smoke (Days 4–5): ingest pipeline + KMS logging verified; no high-severity findings
- QA validation (Days 6–10): 20 curated prompts + 200 automated PII tests; <= 2 critical QA faults and <= 10 non-critical issues
- Readiness review (Day 11): metrics review and Exec signoff

Pass thresholds (final):
- Latency: P95 <= 450ms (evaluation window). Improvement plan to 350ms within 30 days post-contract documented in MAP
- Quality: >= 90% human parity on the curated prompt set
- Cost: trial token cost < $0.06 per session
- Reliability: >= 99.5% successful completions at 10 rps

Remediation & rollback triggers:
- If P95 > 600ms or > 5 critical QA failures => automatic rollback to compatibility model and immediate remediation sprint (48–72h)

Action items and owners:
- Naomi / StellarHealth: confirm QA lead (Sandra) and provide sample dataset by Nov 18
- Markus / Redwood: update acceptance_tests.yml and provide remediation GH issues by Nov 17
- Aditya / Redwood: create the HubSpot task and attach the MAP workbook (DEAL-8743) by Nov 16
- Olga / Redwood: schedule checkpoint review for Nov 23 (kickoff) and Nov 30 (final metrics review)

Attachments: redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx, acceptance_tests.yml
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-8743

Please reply with a single line approval ("StellarHealth approves MAP v1") or proposed edits by EOD Nov 18 so we can lock the SOW timeline.

Thanks — looking forward to kicking this off.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
